newsitem.title: FINLAND: Bank of Finland seen selling markka - dealers.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Finland seen selling markka - dealers.

text.p: The Bank of Finland intervened on the foreign exchange market on Tuesday selling markka for German marks, forex dealers in Helsinki told Reuters.
"The Bank of Finland has been selling markka for marks," one senior currency dealer said. A central bank official declined comment.
At 1445 (1145 GMT), the markka traded at 3.0130 against the mark, unchanged compared to Monday's close but off its intra-day high of 3.0115.

The markka started to firm on Monday, boosted by Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen's view that the time was ripe for a decision in the near future on a markka-ERM link and that no manipulation of the exchange rate would be possible prior to any link.
